headline: High: oh-my-openagent’s broad networked, MCP-driven defaults can leak or misapply LlamaFactory-derived outputs; prompt-injection risk is lower because LlamaFactory has no I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory exposes no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly inject into oh-my-openagent. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of content into oh-my-openagent’s runtime-injected MCP/hooks environment, which is an unusual configuration. Because the pairwise pathway is indirect and one-sided, severity stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies LlamaFactory output into oh-my-openagent prompts or hooks, injection becomes possible.
IF oh-my-openagent treats pasted content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste from model outputs into agent prompts during review.
Add a fixed delimiter/template for pasted content.
Require a human to summarize LlamaFactory output before reuse.
Turn off runtime-injected MCPs for the session if not needed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LlamaFactory touches no data classes and has no egress, but oh-my-openagent touches project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, session history, and provider auth data, with broad network egress. If LlamaFactory outputs are fed into oh-my-openagent, that content can be transmitted to third parties or logged. The interaction is inferred, but the leakage path is plausible in default use of the networked agent.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory outputs contain secrets or sensitive project text and are pasted into oh-my-openagent, leakage can occur.
IF oh-my-openagent sends session context to external APIs, imported content may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets into oh-my-openagent.
Use a redaction pass before transferring any LlamaFactory output.
Restrict oh-my-openagent network access for sensitive sessions.
Review provider logs and disable retention where possible.
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive workflows to a local-only agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files or modify git state, so it cannot conflict on shared mutable resources by itself. oh-my-openagent can write to config and plugin paths and supports multiple instances per installation, which creates overlap if an operator routes LlamaFactory-generated edits back into the same workspace. The conflict is not default for LlamaFactory, but the writable surfaces on oh-my-openagent make the pair moderately risky.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or config directory, concurrent edits can collide.
IF oh-my-openagent instances run simultaneously, writes to shared config paths can race.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same repo.
Back up config files before editing.
Use a single active oh-my-openagent instance per installation.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LlamaFactory can generate model outputs, and oh-my-openagent is designed to act on code/search/tooling context with MCP hooks. If the latter treats imported text as authoritative, errors from LlamaFactory can cascade into tool actions or code changes. Because no verification workflow is documented in the profiles, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent uses LlamaFactory output as instructions or facts without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF the output is used to drive code edits or tool calls, a single hallucination can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on LlamaFactory output.
Cross-check factual claims against source files.
Use a checklist for any tool-triggering instruction.
Limit oh-my-openagent to read-only mode for review tasks.
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: LlamaFactory is open-source and appears local-only, while oh-my-openagent handles provider auth prompts, session history, and broad network egress. If regulated or sensitive data is processed through the pair, the networked agent can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR controls, so uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into oh-my-openagent, provider-side retention or transfer may violate policy.
IF the operator expects local-only handling, broad egress can create an unreviewed compliance gap.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of oh-my-openagent.
Review provider retention settings before use.
Use a local-only workflow for sensitive tasks.
Document data classes allowed in each agent.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
